To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Facebook is the most popular social media for brand related user generated visual content and for brand related user-generated content in general; Facebook is the most suitable social media for brand-related UGC with a high level of self-presentation, brand centrality and brand recommendation; Twitter and YouTube are the most suitable social medias for brand-related UCG with a high level brand connection with personal experiences; Twitter is the most suitable for brand-related UG with high levels of sharing while purchasing or using the brand,
the differences in brand related UGC across social media are not only still present, but also more pronounced than ever before.

Facebook and Twitter are becoming more similar to YouTube in terms of visual and richer content (e.g. pictures and videos), whereas they are still different from YouTube in terms of real time and ubiquitous content (e.g., location sharing, sharing in response to a marketing campaign) and in terms of content related to the brand (e.g. brand connection with personal life experiences, response to a marketing communication).
